title: Pilot TTFT & tail latency shift review - HelixAI sync
summary: Weekly POC check-in focused on an observed shift in tail latency for the pilot. Reviewed TTFT regressions after recent kernel change, streaming handshake timeouts, and sequence-length distribution impact. Agreed on immediate mitigations (short-term hedging and fallback to quantized variant), deliverables (benchmark spreadsheet + kernel traces), and scheduling a kernel deep-dive next week.
next_steps: Redwood to share annotated perf sheet and latest kernel traces (Priya) by 2026-05-09
HelixAI to run 1000-sample tail test with pinned quantized model and share results by 2026-05-11
Schedule kernel-deep-dive (deep SE session) w/ Redwood by 2026-05-12
action_items: Priya Shah (Redwood) - upload kernel traces + annotated perf spreadsheet - 2026-05-09
Jordan Park (HelixAI) - run tail test with pinned quantized variant and share csv - 2026-05-11
Alex Nguyen (Redwood) - send follow-up email with SSO/SOC2 snapshot and security note - 2026-05-08
transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-05-07
- Time: 09:30 PT
- Duration: 47 minutes
- Attendees: Alex Nguyen (Redwood AE); Priya Shah (Redwood SE); Jordan Park (HelixAI, CTO); Maya Rivera (HelixAI, ML Eng); Samir Khan (HelixAI, Infra)

Summary (auto): quick sync to triage a spike in tail latency after the Tuesday kernel roll. Priya walked through traces, group discussed mitigations and rolling fallback.

00:00 Jordan Park: yeah thanks everyone for hopping on, we saw a couple of SLO hits overnight so wanted to figure out whether this is the kernel change you mentioned or something in our client side buffering.
00:18 Alex Nguyen: yup thanks Jordan. Priya's gonna share the traces she pulled from your pilot cluster and then we can talk about mitigations. quick reminder, goal is to keep TTFT under 180ms p50 and tail below 500ms for the demo.
00:33 Priya Shah: hey all, I pulled the traces and there's a clear shift. the median TTFT is steady but the 99th jumped from ~420ms to about 610ms after the kernel bump. there are signs of backpressure in the streaming handshake path, and a few packets where the first token arrived but the streaming buffer flush delayed emission.
00:56 Maya Rivera: can you say a bit more about "kernel bump"? We only saw a patch that touched fused attention kernels last week.
01:10 Priya Shah: yeah this was the patch that switched some heads to the new fused rotary-attn kernel on the newer machine profile, it's faster on avg but we've seen variance in corner cases where seqlen changes and kv cache warming overlaps with batching windows.
01:32 Samir Khan: interesting, our traffic has been spikier because we enabled a new websocket proxy and some clients have longer seqlens for certain chat flows. that could change the batching and cause microbursts.
01:47 Alex Nguyen: exactly microbursts + seqlen variance is a classic combo. two quick clarifications: are you on hosted pilot pool or dedicated?
01:58 Jordan Park: dedicated pool with reserved capacity, so we control autoscaling but want predictable latency.
02:06 Priya Shah: okay good to know. so the hypothesis: the fused-attn kernel produces a lower avg but higher variance when sequence length shifts mid-batch, plus streaming handshake adds ~30-80ms on some flows.
02:21 Maya Rivera: the handshake — is that the client websocket ACK or the runtime streaming flush?
02:28 Priya Shah: runtime flush — we found a couple flows where the flush waits for a small additional batch before emitting to preserve token order and that introduced extra jitter. transcription note: sometimes the trace labels "flush" as "fush" — audio/transcription artifact.
02:46 Jordan Park: so what are the short-term mitigations we can try before we revert the kernel?
02:52 Priya Shah: quick wins: 1) enable hedging for first-token with a small timeout (eg 60ms) to spin up a fallback path; 2) pin to the quantized variant of the model for your high-seqlen flows; 3) reduce streaming handshake batching threshold to force earlier flushes for real-time flows.
03:12 Alex Nguyen: to add: we can also route high-priority flows to a lower-latency model variant or different machine profile temporarily while we root-cause. that's a policy routing change, low risk.
03:24 Samir Khan: policy routing sounds okay, we'd need a safe rollout plan and a way to monitor cost impact.
03:31 Jordan Park: cost is fine for demo, we just need reliability. what about KV cache warmup? could that be the culprit?
03:40 Priya Shah: we saw a few traces where the KV cache miss on the second request added 80-120ms. that correlates with your client flows that do short burst sequences followed by long context. so yes, cache warmup + fused kernel variance + streaming flush = tail spike.
03:58 Maya Rivera: ok that makes sense. do you have a perf sheet we can review?
04:04 Priya Shah: yes I uploaded a live sheet, link in the chat: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-link/helix-pilot-perf - includes p50/p95/p99 pre/post kernel patch and sample traces. note: some model names got mangled in the export, e.g., "redwood-llm-v2" shows up as "redwood-l m v two" in one csv.
04:30 Jordan Park: got it, will review. can you walk us through one of the traces?
04:35 Priya Shah: sure. trace 7 (cherry-picked) shows a 720ms TTFT. timeline: request received -> batching wait 22ms -> kernel exec 78ms -> streaming flush wait 312ms -> client ack + emit 310ms. the streaming flush wait is the bulk.
04:53 Alex Nguyen: that flush wait is high. we need to know why the runtime waited — policy? buffer threshold? backpressure from downstream?
05:03 Priya Shah: our trace shows the runtime held emission because the batch queue expected more tokens to keep GPU utilization high, but because your flow had a single long sequence, it kept waiting. this is an issue with the batching policy not recognizing high-priority real-time flows.
05:20 Samir Khan: This batch policy — can we tag certain calls as low-latency so they skip the batching window?
05:26 Priya Shah: yes, we support priority tagging and can force immediate flush for those calls. however that increases tokens per second on the device and could affect throughput. tradeoff.
05:36 Jordan Park: for the demo we prefer latency. let's enable priority tag for our interactive endpoints.
05:42 Alex Nguyen: noted. we'll prepare a rollout with a canary. Priya, can you add the policy change to action items?
05:50 Priya Shah: added.
05:53 Maya Rivera: one more question — the fallback path you mentioned: is that a whole different model or a kernel revert?
05:59 Priya Shah: short-term fallback would be to the quantized variant or to the previous fused-attn kernel build — quantized variant tends to have smaller memory footprints and more stable tail in our tests. kernel rollback is heavier and impacts throughput.
06:12 Jordan Park: quantized variant sounds easiest. do we lose quality?
06:16 Priya Shah: small quality delta on certain phrasing but we can run your existing eval prompts through both and show differences. Redwood Optimize will produce a quality delta report.
06:28 Alex Nguyen: action plan suggestion: 1) immediate: enable priority tagging for interactive flows; 2) enable hedging timeout for first-token; 3) pin a small subset of traffic to quantized variant; 4) schedule deeper kernel trace review.
06:44 Samir Khan: agreed. what's hedging latency? you said 60ms earlier — can you explain how that interacts with first-token?
06:50 Priya Shah: hedging fires a parallel request to a fallback after the timeout. so if the primary path doesn't produce first-token within 60ms, the fallback (quantized or simpler kernel) will be attempted in parallel and the earliest first-token wins. downside is duplicate compute cost for those hedged requests.
07:10 Jordan Park: what's our estimate of added cost at 1% hedging?
07:15 Alex Nguyen: rough ballpark: 1% hedging -> ~1% extra token cost + a little overhead for duplicate start. given demo sizing it's acceptable. we'll put numbers in the sheet.
07:27 Maya Rivera: regarding sequence length distribution, we can share a sample of 10k requests so you can see percentiles.
07:33 Jordan Park: yes we'll export a seqlen sample and upload. Samir will do that.
07:38 Samir Khan: I'll export and drop in the shared drive by EOD.
07:42 Priya Shah: thanks. one other finding: a small fraction of requests hit GC/compaction pauses on the host; we saw host-level CPU spikes correlated with the high tail. not the majority but worth checking.
07:56 Samir Khan: we recently upgraded a sidecar that does logging compression; could be related, we'll check.
08:02 Alex Nguyen: good catch. 
08:05 Jordan Park: any security or compliance questions on these changes? the priority tag or routing changes — do they affect auditability?
08:12 Priya Shah: no impact on audit logs; we log routing decisions and model variant used per request. for SOC 2/SSO/KMS, Alex will send the snapshot of our current attestations.
08:22 Alex Nguyen: I'll send the SOC2 summary and KMS integration note after this call.
08:27 Maya Rivera: perfect.
08:29 Priya Shah: plan for the kernel deep-dive: we'll pull full kernel flame traces for the high-tail requests, compare the fused-attn vs previous kernel behavior under varying seqlen and batching. need a 90 minute session with your infra + our SEs. proposed 2026-05-12.
08:48 Jordan Park: sounds good, let's do 5/12 at 10am PT. Samir and Maya will attend.
08:56 Alex Nguyen: scheduled tentatively. I'll send the calendar invite after the meeting.
09:01 Priya Shah: quick note on instrumentation: please enable the per-route token-level tracing flag for two hours during off-peak so we can collect richer traces without large cost. it's enabled on your pilot but it's currently sampling at 0.5% — bump to 5% for the window.
09:17 Samir Khan: ok we'll bump to 5% for two hours tomorrow night.
09:21 Jordan Park: anything else?
09:23 Maya Rivera: for validation, we'll run a 1k-sample tail test against the quantized pinned variant once you share the perf sheet.
09:30 Priya Shah: I'll share the annotated perf sheet + kernel traces by Saturday 5/9. note in the sheet there are a couple of mis-labeled traces and csv encoding weirdness — ignore the ones that say "N/A" in model name.
09:41 Alex Nguyen: and I'll follow up with SSO/SOC2 docs and a succinct note on cost impact for hedging and priority routing.
09:49 Jordan Park: great. recap of immediate next steps?
09:52 Alex Nguyen: Priya to upload traces and sheet (5/9). Helix to export seqlen sample and run quantized tail test (5/11). Schedule kernel deep-dive 5/12. Ramp tracing to 5% for two hours tomorrow. Action items captured in the notes.
10:12 Meeting end.

Transcript notes: occasional speaker mislabels (Speaker 2 vs Priya), minor transcription errors ("fush" vs "flush"). The conversation included real-time decision to hedge first-token and pin to quantized variant. References: perf sheet link (see above), tentative calendar invite for kernel deep-dive, and security artifact to be emailed by Alex.
